sections.text: Apple announced plans to alter macOS privacy settings, requiring very explicit user action before apps gain full-disk access. articles.standfirst: John Steinbeck’s hometown of Salinas is the least affordable city in the US for the middle class, a recent Brookings Institution analysis found

gist: Salinas faces a severe affordability crisis, making homeownership and basic needs difficult for the middle class.
A local rent-stabilization policy divided residents before heading to a referendum vote in November.
Local officials are working to boost job opportunities and support first-time homebuyers.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Salinas became the least affordable city in the country for the middle class. The city council passed a rent stabilization policy in 2024 to help struggling households, but a new board repealed it the following year, leading to a planned referendum vote.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Residents struggle with high housing costs and low wages, forcing multiple families to share small spaces. The situation mirrors broader national affordability struggles and highlights the widening gap between living costs and earnings.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Voters will decide the fate of rent stabilization in a November referendum. Meanwhile, local leaders are trying to expand job prospects and assist first-time buyers.

Stagnant wages combined with surging housing costs and limited supply.

articles.title: UK urged to act as Polymarket takes bets on whether HSBC and Lloyds will fail
articles.standfirst: Revelation comes amid mounting concern over online prediction market’s effects on integrity of financial system

gist: Polymarket is hosting bets on whether major banks like HSBC and Lloyds will fail.
UK authorities are urged to intervene due to risks of market manipulation and bank runs.
Regulators warn prediction markets face high risks of insider trading and corrupt actions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Polymarket has allowed users to place $77,507 worth of bets on whether major global banks, including HSBC and Lloyds, will fail by the end of this year. Although UK, US, Canada, and EU residents are banned from the platform, offshore users can still participate.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Critics warn these bets could trigger social media-fuelled bank runs or encourage market manipulation. The European Securities and Markets Authority warned that prediction markets are rife with insider trading. However, Polymarket argues it democratises access to public financial information.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Liberal Democrat MP Bobby Dean has urged UK regulators to contact US counterparts to address these risks. The Financial Conduct Authority has been speaking to international regulators about prediction markets to protect market integrity.

articles.standfirst: Her last novel sold 5m copies and was adapted into a hit series. Nearly 10 years on, the Korean-American author has written another epic. She discusses ambition and the diagnosis that inspired her to leave work and write

gist: Author Min Jin Lee is releasing her third novel, focusing on Korean education and diaspora.
Lee began writing after a health diagnosis made her fear she would die young.
Her upcoming book is part of a planned four-novel series about the Korean diaspora.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Author Min Jin Lee is publishing her third novel, American Hagwon, which explores the Korean diaspora and the intense culture of private cram schools. Lee, who left her career as a corporate lawyer in 1995 following a serious health diagnosis, has spent decades writing epic novels that bring immigrant experiences to the mainstream.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Lee's previous bestseller, Pachinko, sold over five million copies globally and was adapted for television. Her work, alongside fellow writers like Nobel laureate Han Kang, highlights overlooked periods of Korean history. Lee's sprawling novels challenge the "tiger mom" stereotype and examine the true costs of elite education systems.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Now healthy thanks to experimental drugs, the 57-year-old author plans to write a fourth novel, titled Marshall Plan, focusing on Korean miners and nurses sent to West Germany in 1963.
